Consult Summary:
- Patient presented with acute left-sided throbbing headache starting at mid-day, preceded by visual zig-zag lines and blurred vision, associated with photophobia and two episodes of vomiting; no focal neurological symptoms; clinician impression was migraine; advised analgesics/NSAIDs, headache diary, safety-netting, and follow-up.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Severe left-sided throbbing headache since mid-day today.
- Onset/duration: Began mid-day; a few hours prior to consultation. Patient unsure if sudden or gradual.
- Course/progression: Ongoing at time of consult; worse with leaning forward and head/neck movement.
- Aura/visual symptoms: Visual zig-zag lines and blurred vision a few minutes before headache onset; reported as affecting both eyes; currently light-sensitive (wearing sunglasses).
- Associated symptoms: Nausea with two episodes of vomiting today; photophobia.
- Pertinent negatives: No fever; no rash; no speech difficulty; no limb numbness/weakness; no balance/coordination problems; no recent head injury; no breathlessness.
- Prior episodes: Similar headache a few weeks ago lasting a couple of days; required rest and painkillers; missed work.
- Patient concerns: Significant anxiety about brain tumor due to friend’s mother’s recent death from brain tumor.
- Systems review (documented): Negative as above; otherwise unremarkable.

Past Medical History:
- No known medical conditions reported.
- No prior diagnosis of migraine reported.

Medications:
- Microgynon (combined oral contraceptive) — dose/route/frequency not documented; duration 3 months; for contraception.
- Analgesics (unspecified) used during prior episode — dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Allergies: Not documented.

Social History:
- Occupation: Works in the fashion industry; reports high job stress and managerial pressure.
- Living situation: Lives alone; coping “fine.”
- Exercise: None reported.
- Stress management: None reported.
- Tobacco: Denies.
- Alcohol: Denies.

Family History:
- Mother: Migraines; underactive thyroid.
- No family history of brain cancer reported.

Physical Examination:
- Vitals: Not documented.
- Examination findings: Not documented (examination was proposed but no findings recorded).

Investigations:
- None documented.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Acute unilateral headache consistent with migraine with aura
  - Assessment: Left-sided throbbing headache with visual aura, photophobia, nausea/vomiting; no red-flag neurological features; clinician reassured patient that meningitis and brain cancer are unlikely based on history.
  - Plan:
    - Analgesia: Paracetamol or co-codamol (dose/route/frequency not documented).
    - Anti-inflammatory options: Ibuprofen or naproxen (dose/route/frequency not documented).
    - Headache diary to identify triggers.
    - Consider prophylactic migraine medication if headaches become persistent; to be discussed at follow-up.
    - Follow-up: Next week.
    - Safety-netting: Return/seek care if not improving in 2–3 days or if worsening headache, non-response to meds, worsening neck pain, new limb weakness, vision changes, or other concerning symptoms.

- Issue 2: Health anxiety regarding brain tumor
  - Assessment: Patient highly anxious due to friend’s mother’s brain tumor; reassurance provided based on clinical features.
  - Plan:
    - Education and reassurance provided; advised to return if red-flag symptoms develop.

- Issue 3: Work-related stress impacting function
  - Assessment: High occupational stress; recent missed work due to headache.
  - Plan:
    - No specific intervention documented; to reassess at follow-up.

- General Plan items:
  - None additional documented.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements: Allergies not documented; vital signs absent; physical/neuro exam findings not documented; medication doses/routes/frequencies not documented; past surgical history not obtained.
- Internal conflicts: None significant; patient was unsure about onset speed; visual symptoms affirmed as both eyes by clinician after patient said “yeah.”
- Transcript quality: Generally clear; minor mishearing noted (“Lyme’s disease” reference by clinician not corroborated by patient); examination discussed but not recorded.
